title: OpenMP I: shared-memory threads and the distribution of work
transcript_provenance: Local machine transcription (faster-whisper small.en); not publisher captions
source_uncertainties: Dagum and Menon (1998), IEEE Comput. Sci. Eng. 5(1) 46-55: the full text and the IEEE Xplore abstract page could not be opened (the page returned an empty body to scripted clients on 2026-10-26). The bibliographic data were checked in Crossref (DOI 10.1109/99.660313; pages 46-55; volume 5, issue 1) and the abstract text was read through the OpenAlex record. The chapter cites the paper for abstract-level statements only and relies on no other claim of the paper.

Menon (1998) Cray User Group slides: slide 5 gives Fortran v1.0 specification October 1997 and C/C++ v1.0 specification August 1998. The slides carry no date, so it is not known whether the C/C++ date was planned or achieved when the talk was given. The chapter says so.

Amdahl (1967) was read in the 2007 IEEE SSCS News reprint (redrawn figure); the reprint's editors state the paper has no equations. The AFIPS original was not opened. The formula S = 1/(f + (1-f)/p) is presented as a later formalization derived in the chapter; the chapter's remark that 1/f gives 5 and 7.5 for housekeeping fractions of 0.20 and 0.133 is the author's reading of the paper's 'five to seven', not a statement of the paper.

OpenMP 5.2 (November 2021) is the document cited for definitions. gcc 13.3 reports _OPENMP = 201511 (version 4.5). OpenMP 6.0 was not opened, so the chapter does not claim that the data-race wording is unchanged there. Page numbers are the printed page numbers of the 5.2 PDF (PDF page minus 20).

Drepper (2007): the chapter reads 'overhead computed by dividing the time with a single cache line by the time with a separate cache line per thread is 390%, 734% and 1,147%' as time ratios of 3.9, 7.3 and 11.5. His text gives the percentages and the division, not the word 'ratio'.

Statements about the libgomp runtime (thread reuse between regions) rest on the author's timings only; the libgomp documentation on thread pools was not opened (only the GOMP_SPINCOUNT page was). The explanation that gcc -O2 keeps sum[id*stride] in a register was first inferred from timings; in round 3 the assembly of gcc 13.3 (gcc -O2 -fopenmp -S pi_scaling.c, in WSL) showed the partial sum zeroed in a register before the loop, added to inside the loop, and stored once after it.

ASR errors in the machine transcript corrected from slides: the transcript gives the four-thread time of the lecture's table as '2.97 seconds'; the slide reads 0.97. 'OMP-setnum-threads' = omp_set_num_threads; 'poo' = pooh; 'CIDR file' = header file. The slide's code prints num_steps = 100000 while its timing line says 100000000 steps; the chapter takes 10^8 from the timing line and says so. The slide's sum runs from i = 0 to N (N+1 terms) while the code runs N terms.

The lecture's hello-world runs were on a MacBook (gcc-14 visible in a frame) with 8 processing cores per the lecturer's statement; the chapter uses only what was stated or shown. The lecturer's remark that the timing-study average should be taken over about five runs is reported as stated.
Timestamps are section anchors from local speech-recognition segment times and locate topic changes to within a few seconds.

Hybrid processor (Intel ARK, retrieved 2026-10-26): 4 P-cores x 2 threads + 4 E-cores x 1 thread; max turbo 4.40 / 3.30 GHz. The author's own fetch of the ARK page returned HTTP 403; the page was opened by the reviewer, and a web search returned consistent core counts, thread counts and turbo frequencies from secondary sources (Notebookcheck, TechPowerUp). WSL 2 shows a synthetic 6 cores x 2 threads; placement was not controlled. Explanations given as consistent with the data but not tested: (a) the speedup plateau near 3.7-4.4 for the pi loop, as S_p = p v_min with equal shares (copies, final session: v_min 0.87, 0.75, 0.49, 0.41 for 2, 4, 8, 12; at p = 12 the threaded loop reaches 80 % of C_12, a gap not explained; the best-of-5 rule of the copies may overstate C_12); (b) S_24 slightly above S_12 and the 100/1000-thread runs, as oversubscription that moves S toward the sum of per-processor speeds; (c) the region-cost rise at p = 10-12 (in the final sample the cost at p = 10 still follows the trend and the rise starts at p = 11), as preemption of spinning team threads (libgomp spin count 300,000 when OMP_WAIT_POLICY is undefined) when all logical processors are occupied; it does not start at p = 9, so it is not a topology effect; (d) cyclic S above p in earlier triangle.c runs (2.11 at p = 2, 4.27 at p = 4), as a slow one-thread reference; (e) the non-monotone unpadded -O0 time at p = 8, 12, 24, as fewer concurrent writers per cache line when 24 threads are time-sliced on 12 processors. Still unexplained: the one-line penalty for 4-byte counters (2.9-3.0 times) against 8-byte counters (2.0-2.6 times).

The machine was shared with other jobs (other agents) during the final capture of all timing samples and timing sessions (first regions of 1000 threads, single runs, independent copies). The hello-world output counts (1619 123 114 99 18 10 8 6 2 1; 112) come from an earlier session and were not recaptured. Every speed is therefore lower by an unknown amount and the run-to-run variation is wider than on an idle machine. The chapter says so in the section on the model and in the limits. Numbers quoted as 'earlier runs' come from earlier sessions with the same programs or earlier versions of them (for example the first parallel region cost 6-28 ms in eight runs; the one-line false-sharing ratio at p = 8 was 2.0-2.6 in four runs; the cyclic speedup of triangle.c at p = 4 was 3.54, 3.84 and 4.27 in three runs) and are not reproduced by a listing.

A hung process from an earlier out-of-range experiment (5000 threads writing past a 64-slot array; the experiment was dropped) was present in WSL during the first timing runs of the first draft and was gone before the final captures of the revision.

sections.section: The objects of the chapter and the running case
sections.teaching_construction: Formal model: events, program order, fork, join, schedules, storage (shared/private), cost of a region; symbol list; machine description.

sections.section: OpenMP is directives, a runtime library and environment variables
sections.lecture_material: API of directives, library routines and environment variables; legacy-code motivation; solution stack; common core of 21 items; directive syntax and structured block; omp.h and -fopenmp.
sections.research_extension: Dagum and Menon 1998 (abstract); Menon 1998 slides (specification dates); OpenMP 5.2 sections 1.3, 3.3, 4.3.
sections.teaching_construction: Scope of the chapter within the common core; reading of a directive as a change of meaning.

sections.section: A first parallel program, its many outputs and the interleaving model
sections.lecture_material: Hello world in a parallel region; output varies between runs; 8, 4 and 24 threads; concurrency and parallelism definitions.
sections.teaching_construction: Count of schedules (2p)!/2^p and outputs (Catalan numbers); enumeration program; 2000-run experiment.

sections.section: Fork-join execution and the size of the team
sections.lecture_material: Fork-join model and nested regions; team size from an environment variable; omp_set_num_threads; thread number; hello world with thread number.
sections.teaching_construction: team.c checking precedence and thread numbers; correction of 'operating system' to the runtime ICV.

sections.section: Shared and private storage, redundant execution and the data race
sections.lecture_material: Parallel region with pooh(ID, A); redundant execution; shared array and private ID; implicit barrier; requested versus actual threads; scalar promoted to array to avoid a race.
sections.research_extension: OpenMP 5.2 sections 5.1.1 and 1.4.1 (data-race definition, update granularity).
sections.teaching_construction: Model definition of a race; race.c; remark that race-freedom (memory units) and false sharing (cache lines) are independent.

sections.section: The midpoint rule for pi: cost and error
sections.lecture_material: Integral of 4/(1+x^2) as a sum of rectangles; serial program; omp_get_wtime.
sections.research_extension: OpenStax Calculus Volume 2 section 3.6 Theorem 3.5 (error bound).
sections.teaching_construction: Derivation of the bound and of the h^2/24 [f'] expansion; M = 8; h^2/12 for this f; cost-accuracy budget; pi_error.c.

sections.section: The SPMD program: cyclic and block distribution of iterations
sections.lecture_material: SPMD pi program with sum[id], thread 0 copying the team size, serial global sum, cyclic and block distribution.
sections.research_extension: OpenMP 5.2 section 1.3 (different numbers of threads, different numeric results).
sections.teaching_construction: Dependence argument and reduction; distributions; load-balance model (11.3), (11.4); pi_spmd.c; triangle.c.

sections.lecture_material: Timing table 1.86/1.03/1.08/0.97 s; speedup, linear and superlinear; Amdahl's law with alpha.
sections.research_extension: Amdahl 1967 (argument, 40 percent housekeeping, five to seven times; no equations).
sections.teaching_construction: Derivation from assumptions A1-A3; experimental serial fraction; two-core model; amdahl.py.

sections.section: The cost of a parallel region and the choice of the thread count
sections.lecture_material: Overheads of thread creation, destruction and management; 1000 threads slower than serial; OMP_NUM_THREADS without recompiling; timing study.
sections.teaching_construction: Overhead model and optimum team size; fork_cost.c; single-shot 1000-thread runs; capacity-plus-creation model; selection procedure.

sections.section: False sharing: cache-line arithmetic and a measurement
sections.research_extension: Drepper 2007 sections 3.2, 6.4.1 (64-byte lines, write ownership, measured penalties).
sections.teaching_construction: Line-index formula (11.8); falseshare.c; pi_scaling.c with -O0/-O2 and strides 1/8; independent-copies capacity measurement.

sections.section: What the model establishes and what it does not

sections.teaching_construction: Six exercises with full solutions: derive, compute, counterexample, diagnose an assumption, design judgment, implementation and measurement.

references.title: Lecture W4L1 recording
references.supports: Parallel regions, pi by the midpoint rule, SPMD with cyclic and block distribution, timing table, speedup and Amdahl's law, overhead.

references.title: OpenMP Application Programming Interface, Version 5.2 (November 2021)
references.supports: p. 23-24: fork-join, implicit barrier, nested region with one thread when nesting is disabled, different numbers of threads may give different numeric results; p. 27: update granularity, definition of data race, result unspecified; p. 69: _OPENMP is yyyymm; p. 76: structured blocks; p. 97: automatic variables declared inside the construct are private; p. 99: variables referenced in a parallel construct without default clause are shared; p. 223: team creation, thread numbers consecutive from zero, team size constant; p. 226-227: Algorithm 2.1 for the number of threads; p. 348-349: omp_set_num_threads, omp_get_num_threads; p. 413-414: omp_get_wtime per-thread time; p. 600: OMP_NUM_THREADS sets nthreads-var.
references.page_checked: text extracted from the PDF (669 pages); printed page numbers = PDF page minus 20

references.title: Amdahl, Validity of the single processor approach to achieving large scale computing capabilities (AFIPS 1967; 2007 IEEE SSCS News reprint)
references.supports: Housekeeping is 40 percent of executed instructions, might be halved but not reduced by a factor of three; overhead alone limits throughput to five to seven times; the reprint's editors state the paper has no equations and one figure.
references.page_checked: both pages of the reprint (pp. 19-20 of the newsletter)

references.title: Dagum and Menon, OpenMP: an industry standard API for shared-memory programming, IEEE Computational Science & Engineering 5(1), 1998, pp. 46-55
references.supports: Abstract: OpenMP is a set of compiler directives and callable runtime library routines extending Fortran (and separately C and C++) to express shared-memory parallelism; it builds on X3H5 concepts and extends them to coarse-grain parallelism; the standard includes a runtime library with environment variables.
references.page_checked: abstract only (via the OpenAlex record); bibliographic data via Crossref; full text not opened

references.title: Menon, OpenMP Application Program Interface, slides, Cray User Group 1998
references.supports: Slide 5: Fortran v1.0 specification October 1997, C/C++ v1.0 specification August 1998.
references.page_checked: all 17 slides read as extracted text; slide 5

references.title: OpenStax, Calculus Volume 2, section 3.6 Numerical Integration
references.supports: Theorem 3.5, eq. 3.12: for f continuous with a second derivative bounded by M on [a,b], the midpoint-rule error is at most M(b-a)^3/(24 n^2).

references.title: Drepper, What every programmer should know about memory (2007)
references.supports: p. 15 (section 3.2): cache lines of 64 bytes are the norm; pp. 65-67 (section 6.4.1): writes to a shared line need exclusive state and many request-for-ownership messages; false sharing measured at 390%, 734% and 1,147% (one line against one line per thread, 2-4 threads) on four Pentium 4 processors; no growing penalty on a single-processor quad-core Core 2.

references.title: Intel, Intel Core i5-12450H processor specifications (ARK)
references.supports: Total cores 8: 4 performance cores (2 threads each) and 4 efficient cores (1 thread each); 12 threads; maximum turbo frequency 4.40 GHz (P-core) and 3.30 GHz (E-core); launched Q1 2022.
references.page_checked: retrieved 2026-10-26 (opened by the reviewer; the author's fetch returned HTTP 403; consistent figures from secondary sources via web search)

references.title: GNU libgomp manual, GOMP_SPINCOUNT
references.supports: A waiting thread spins 300,000 times when OMP_WAIT_POLICY is undefined (30 billion for ACTIVE, 0 for PASSIVE); if there are more OpenMP threads than available CPUs, 1000 spins (ACTIVE) and 100 spins (undefined).
references.page_checked: full page text, online edition for the current GCC release, retrieved 2026-10-26; the chapter assumes that the libgomp of gcc 13.3 has the same default
